> **Model C — boolean composition over 15 facets (per [ADR-078](../../adr/adr-078-orgpath-attribute-schema-15-facet.qmd)).** Membership rules compose facet predicates (`attr2 -eq "IT" and attr3 -eq "CyberOps"`) instead of text-parsing a single composite path. See [OrgPath Codebook](codebook.qmd) for the facet/slot model.

## Why Dynamic Groups Matter

In Active Directory, group membership was a manual operation. An administrator added a user to a security group, and that membership persisted until someone remembered to remove it. Transfer to a new department? Hope someone updated the groups. Leave the organization? Hope the offboarding checklist included every group. The result: group sprawl, stale memberships, and access control that drifted from organizational reality within weeks of any personnel change.

Entra ID dynamic groups solve this — membership is computed from user attributes, not manually assigned. When a facet value changes (because HR updated the department), every dynamic group membership recalculates automatically. No tickets, no manual steps, no drift.

But dynamic groups without a governance library are just a different kind of sprawl. Instead of manually-managed groups drifting, you get hundreds of dynamic groups with inconsistent naming, overlapping membership rules, and no canonical source of truth.

The Dynamic Group Library (UIAO_152) is that source of truth.

## Three Composition Patterns

Under Model C, every dynamic group rule in the library uses one of three patterns built from per-facet predicates:

| Pattern | Operator | Use Case | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Single-facet** | `-eq` / `-in` | All users carrying a value (or a value set) in one facet | `(attr2 -eq "IT")` |
| **Multi-facet AND** | `... and ...` | Users matching every clause across multiple facets | `(attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "CyberOps")` |
| **Multi-facet OR / set** | `... or ...` / `-in [...]` | Cross-cutting groupings (multiple departments, role tiers, clearance bands) | `(attr2 -in ["IT","Engineering"])` |

The OR / set form replaces Model A's regex hack and Branch/Node distinction. Branch groups (`-startsWith` across composite-hyphen paths) are not needed in Model C because each facet is already a discrete attribute — you query the facet directly rather than parsing its position inside a string.

## Canonical Group Inventory (per-facet examples)

### Region groups (`extensionAttribute1`)

| Group | Rule | Captures |
|---|---|---|
| `OrgTree-Region-NCR-Users` | `(attr1 -eq "NCR")` | All National Capital Region users |
| `OrgTree-Region-EMEA-Users` | `(attr1 -eq "EMEA")` | All Europe / Middle East / Africa users |
| `OrgTree-Region-US-Users` | `(attr1 -in ["NCR","EASTUS","WESTUS","CENTRAL"])` | All US-region users (composite) |

### Department groups (`extensionAttribute2`)

| Group | Rule | Captures |
|---|---|---|
| `OrgTree-Department-IT-Users` | `(attr2 -eq "IT")` | All IT department users |
| `OrgTree-Department-HR-Users` | `(attr2 -eq "HR")` | All HR users |
| `OrgTree-Department-Finance-Users` | `(attr2 -eq "Finance")` | All Finance users |
| `OrgTree-Department-Executive-Users` | `(attr2 -eq "Executive")` | All Executive users |

### Division groups (`extensionAttribute3` within Department)

| Group | Rule | Captures |
|---|---|---|
| `OrgTree-IT-CyberOps-Users` | `(attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "CyberOps")` | IT/CyberOps division |
| `OrgTree-IT-InfraOps-Users` | `(attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "InfraOps")` | IT/Infrastructure division |
| `OrgTree-IT-AppDev-Users` | `(attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "AppDev")` | IT/Application Development |

### Role-tier groups (`extensionAttribute4`)

| Group | Rule | Captures |
|---|---|---|
| `OrgTree-Role-Managers-Users` | `(attr4 -in ["Manager","Director","VP"])` | All people-management roles |
| `OrgTree-Role-Engineers-Users` | `(attr4 -in ["Engineer","Architect"])` | All engineering ICs |
| `OrgTree-Role-CISO-Users` | `(attr4 -eq "CISO")` | CISO singletons |

### Clearance-gated groups (`extensionAttribute9`)

| Group | Rule | Captures |
|---|---|---|
| `OrgTree-Cleared-Secret-Plus-Users` | `(attr9 -in ["Secret","TopSecret","TS_SCI"])` | All cleared personnel |
| `OrgTree-Cleared-TopSecret-Plus-Users` | `(attr9 -in ["TopSecret","TS_SCI"])` | TS / TS-SCI only |

### Account-type groups (`extensionAttribute10`)

| Group | Rule | Captures |
|---|---|---|
| `OrgTree-AccountType-Privileged-Users` | `(attr10 -eq "Privileged")` | Privileged accounts (PIM-eligible) |
| `OrgTree-AccountType-Service-Users` | `(attr10 -eq "Service")` | Service accounts |
| `OrgTree-AccountType-Guest-Users` | `(attr10 -eq "Guest")` | B2B guests |

### Specialized cross-facet groups

| Group | Rule | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `OrgTree-Executive-CA` | `(attr6 -eq "Executive")` | Executive Conditional Access tier |
| `OrgTree-IT-Security-CA` | `(attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "CyberOps") and (attr10 -eq "Privileged")` | CyberOps privileged-access CA |
| `OrgTree-Executive-Licensed` | `(attr6 -eq "Executive")` | E5 + Copilot licensing |
| `OrgTree-IT-Licensed` | `(attr2 -eq "IT")` | E5 licensing for the IT department |
| `OrgTree-SecurityCompliance-Users` | `(attr2 -eq "IT" and attr3 -eq "CyberOps") or (attr2 -eq "Legal" and attr3 -eq "GRC")` | Cross-functional security/compliance |

### Lifecycle-driven groups (`extensionAttribute7` / `extensionAttribute8`)

| Group | Rule | Captures |
|---|---|---|
| `OrgTree-Active-Employees` | `(attr8 -eq "")` | Empty TermDate ⇒ active |
| `OrgTree-Joiners-Last-30d` | `(attr7 -ge "<today-30d>")` | Recent hires (templated date) |
| `OrgTree-Leavers-Next-30d` | `(attr8 -gt "<today>") and (attr8 -lt "<today+30d>")` | Pre-departure offboarding queue |

## Five Drift Categories for Groups

| Category | What It Means | Severity | Auto-Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rule Drift** | Tenant rule differs from canonical rule | HIGH | Yes |
| **Phantom Group** | `OrgTree-` group exists in tenant but not in library | MEDIUM | No |
| **Missing Group** | Library entry has no corresponding tenant group | HIGH | Yes |
| **Name Drift** | Correct rule, wrong name | LOW | Yes |
| **Membership Drift** | Unexpected member count — root cause is facet values in the codebook (UIAO_151) | MEDIUM | Fix at source |

## Governance Rules

1. **No manual members** — dynamic groups in this library are dynamic-only
2. **One rule per group** — no multi-rule groups; split into separate groups
3. **Deterministic naming** — name derives from facet(s) + value(s) + purpose suffix (e.g., `OrgTree-IT-CyberOps-CA`)
4. **Single-facet preferred** — multi-facet compositions only when the cross-facet selection is operationally distinct
5. **Governed changes only** — additions/modifications follow UIAO_155 Workflow 3
